note.question: How should a bank charge for a penalty-free prepayment option without intensifying the borrower's incentive to refinance or rationing otherwise valuable projects?
note.overview: A competitive bank chooses a loan rate and upfront fee anticipating that a borrower will invest and, after public but noncontractible information arrives, strategically prepay or continue the loan; the paper derives equilibrium contracts and tests their predictions.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At date 0, the bank offers a rate and possibly an upfront fee, and the firm borrows one unit and invests. At interim date theta, a public but noncontractible project-quality signal arrives; a good-news borrower may pay a refinancing cost and prepay, whereas a bad-news borrower continues. At date 1, the project payoff is realized and the loan is repaid if successful. Raising the rate worsens good borrowers' incentive to leave, so rate-only compensation can destroy feasibility.

Under this credit-risk interpretation of the cancellation fee, eliminating loans with a positive cancellation fee from the regression sample should not affect our main prediction of a positive association between upfront fees and our prepayment risk index.
